learning_objective: 🗂️ Turn messy, raw data into a neatly organized structure using variables, tally marks, and frequency distributions!

चर (वह गुण जिसका मान बदल सकता है और जिसे मापा जा सकता है)
आवृत्ति / बारंबारता (कोई मूल्य कितनी बार दोहराया गया है)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Raw data is a messy pile of numbers. Classification is like arranging a messy closet into neat drawers based on similarities. It condenses the data, makes comparisons easy, and highlights important features.

Data can be classified chronologically (by time/years), spatially (by geography/states), qualitatively (by attributes like gender/religion), or quantitatively (by numerical values like height/income).

A Discrete variable takes exact, whole numbers (e.g., number of children in a family: 1, 2, 3 - never 2.5). A Continuous variable can take ANY value in a range, including fractions/decimals (e.g., height, weight, temperature).

A table showing how data is distributed over different class intervals. It consists of classes (like 0-10, 10-20) and their corresponding frequencies (how many items fall in that class), counted using Tally marks.

In an Exclusive series (10-20, 20-30), the upper limit is EXCLUDED from that class (the number 20 goes to the next class). In an Inclusive series (10-19, 20-29), both upper and lower limits are INCLUDED in the same class.

fun_activity.title: |||| The Tally Mark Race
fun_activity.instructions: Take a random paragraph from a book. Count how many times the vowels (A, E, I, O, U) appear using Tally Marks (grouping them in 5s by slashing the 5th line across the first 4). Notice how much faster it is to count the final total when they are grouped in 5s!

exam_tips: 📌 Mid-point (Class Mark) is calculated as: (Upper Limit + Lower Limit) / 2. This is crucial for plotting graphs and calculating means later.
📌 To convert an inclusive series to an exclusive one, subtract 0.5 from the lower limits and add 0.5 to the upper limits.
📌 Magnitude of a class interval (Class width) = Upper Limit - Lower Limit.
quick_recap: ⭐ Raw data is an unorganized mass of various measurements.
⭐ Bivariate frequency distribution shows the frequency distribution of two variables simultaneously (e.g., height and weight of students).
⭐ The number of times a particular observation appears in the data is called its frequency.
